newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ junior minister fired amid coalition tension.
newsitem.headline: NZ junior minister fired amid coalition tension.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Thursday fired a junior cabinet minister, Neil Kirton, after a dispute between ministers from different coalition parties.

Peters, who heads junior coalition party New Zealand First, to which Kirton belongs, told a news conference he had fired Kirton, who was Associate Health Minister and Customs Minister, for breaking an agreement not to speak to the media.
The move followed a drawn-out disagreement over duties between Kirton and senior Health Minister Bill English, who is from the larger party in the centre-right coalition, National.

"Last night I made it very clear to Mr Kirton that there was to be no media comment pending a meeting between the Prime Minister and myself to sort out the public dispute between the two health ministers," Peters said in a statement.
"This morning Mr Kirton went on radio in disregard to that clear instruction and accordingly I have dismissed him," he added.
Peters said he had made the decision with regret and "in the interest of sound government".
The row has its roots in the handling of a number of health policy issues where Kirton has crossed swords with English.
On Wednesday Kirton received a reprimand from Prime Minister Jim Bolger that followed calls from opposition politicians for some form of disciplinary action.
